title: PHYLIP and Phylogenetics Software Timeline
description: Key events in the history of PHYLIP, Joe Felsenstein's contributions, and the phylogenetics software ecosystem

events.title: Joe Felsenstein born
events.description: Joseph Felsenstein born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. Future architect of computational phylogenetics.

events.title: Felsenstein B.S. under James F. Crow
events.description: Felsenstein earns B.S. in Zoology (Honors) from University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under population geneticist James F. Crow.

events.title: Felsenstein joins University of Washington
events.description: Felsenstein joins UW as Assistant Professor of Genetics after completing Ph.D. at University of Chicago under Richard Lewontin.

events.title: Fitch-Margoliash method published
events.description: Walter Fitch and Emanuel Margoliash publish their distance method for constructing phylogenetic trees from protein sequence data.

events.title: Jukes-Cantor model published
events.description: Thomas Jukes and Charles Cantor publish the simplest nucleotide substitution model, assuming equal rates between all nucleotide pairs.
events.citation: Jukes, T.H. & Cantor, C.R. (1969). In Mammalian Protein Metabolism, 21-132.

events.title: Sanger sequencing developed
events.description: Frederick Sanger publishes the chain-termination method for DNA sequencing, making molecular phylogenetics practical.

events.title: Felsenstein proposes ML for phylogenies
events.description: Felsenstein publishes two papers proposing maximum likelihood estimation of phylogenetic trees, for discrete and continuous characters. These contain the first version of the pruning algorithm.

events.title: Felsenstein Zone / Long Branch Attraction
events.description: Felsenstein demonstrates that parsimony can be statistically inconsistent, converging on the wrong tree. Introduces the concept of long branch attraction. Motivates adoption of model-based methods.

events.title: Kimura 2-parameter model published
events.description: Motoo Kimura publishes his two-parameter substitution model distinguishing transitions from transversions.
events.citation: Kimura, M. (1980). Journal of Molecular Evolution, 16, 111-120.

events.title: PHYLIP version 1.0 released
events.description: Joe Felsenstein releases PHYLIP 1.0, distributed on magnetic tapes. Includes parsimony and distance methods written in Pascal. One of the first freely distributed bioinformatics software packages.

events.title: Felsenstein pruning algorithm published
events.description: Felsenstein publishes the pruning algorithm for computing maximum likelihood on phylogenetic trees. This dynamic programming algorithm becomes the mathematical foundation of all modern ML phylogenetics software.
events.citation: Felsenstein, J. (1981). Journal of Molecular Evolution, 17, 368-376.

events.title: Felsenstein 1981 (F81) substitution model
events.description: The same 1981 paper introduces the F81 substitution model, allowing unequal base frequencies.

events.title: GenBank established
events.description: GenBank opens as a public repository of nucleotide sequences at Los Alamos National Laboratory.

events.title: Meacham creates tree format for PHYLIP
events.description: Christopher Meacham creates the tree-drawing format during sabbatical at University of Georgia, for PHYLIP's Drawgram and Drawtree programs. This becomes the basis for the Newick format.

events.title: Phylogenetic bootstrap published
events.description: Felsenstein adapts Efron's bootstrap to phylogenetics, giving the field its first widely adopted measure of tree confidence. The method becomes ubiquitous.

events.title: Phylogenetically independent contrasts published
events.description: Felsenstein publishes PIC, solving the non-independence problem in cross-species comparisons. Becomes the 2nd most cited paper in The American Naturalist (~9,000+ citations).

events.title: PCR invented
events.description: Kary Mullis invents the polymerase chain reaction, revolutionizing molecular biology and enabling the explosion of sequence data that phylogenetics software would analyze.

events.title: Newick format adopted
events.description: Felsenstein convenes committee at SSE meetings in Durham, NH. The standard is finalized at Newick's Lobster House in Dover, NH. Named after the restaurant. Becomes the universal tree format.

events.title: PHYLIP version 3.0 released
events.description: Major expansion of PHYLIP. More programs, improved portability, initial C implementations alongside Pascal.

events.title: Neighbor-joining published
events.description: Naruya Saitou and Masatoshi Nei publish the neighbor-joining algorithm, which becomes the most widely used distance method for tree construction.
events.citation: Saitou, N. & Nei, M. (1987). Molecular Biology and Evolution, 4, 406-425.

events.title: PHYLIP formally cited in Cladistics
events.description: Felsenstein publishes the formal PHYLIP citation paper for version 3.2, providing a citable reference for the thousands of researchers using the package.

events.title: PHYLIP version 3.2 released
events.description: Adds protein sequence analysis and maximum likelihood methods. PHYLIP becomes truly general-purpose.

events.title: World Wide Web created
events.description: Tim Berners-Lee creates the World Wide Web at CERN. Within a few years, Felsenstein's software catalog would become one of the most important scientific resource pages on the early web.

events.title: Felsenstein elected to AAAS
events.description: Joe Felsenstein elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.

events.title: President of SSE; Sewall Wright Award
events.description: Felsenstein serves as President of the Society for the Study of Evolution and receives the Sewall Wright Award.

events.title: PHYLIP version 3.3 — rewritten in C
events.description: PHYLIP source code rewritten from Pascal to C, greatly expanding portability across operating systems including MacOS, Windows, and Linux.

events.title: Software catalog page established
events.description: Felsenstein establishes the phylogenetics software catalog on the web at evolution.genetics.washington.edu. Among the earliest comprehensive scientific software directories on the internet.

events.title: MrBayes development begins
events.description: John Huelsenbeck begins developing MrBayes, which will become the dominant Bayesian phylogenetics program. Built on ideas implemented in PHYLIP.

events.title: Felsenstein elected to NAS
events.description: Joe Felsenstein elected to the National Academy of Sciences.

events.title: Weldon Memorial Prize
events.description: Felsenstein receives the Weldon Memorial Prize from Oxford University.

events.title: Bioconductor launched
events.description: Bioconductor project launched for R-based bioinformatics. PHYLIP's catalog had been serving a similar discovery function for phylogenetics software for 8 years.

events.title: President's Award, Society of Systematic Biology
events.description: Felsenstein receives the President's Award for Excellence in Systematics.

events.title: Inferring Phylogenies published
events.description: Felsenstein publishes his comprehensive textbook with Sinauer Associates, covering the mathematical foundations of all major phylogenetic methods. Becomes the definitive reference in the field.
events.citation: Felsenstein, J. (2004). Inferring Phylogenies. Sinauer Associates.

events.title: Honorary D.Sc., University of Edinburgh
events.description: Felsenstein receives an Honorary Doctor of Science degree from the University of Edinburgh.

events.title: RAxML gains prominence
events.description: Alexandros Stamatakis's RAxML becomes the dominant ML program for large-scale phylogenetics. Uses Felsenstein's pruning algorithm at its core.

events.title: Darwin-Wallace Medal; Carty Award
events.description: Felsenstein receives the Darwin-Wallace Medal from the Linnean Society of London and the John J. Carty Award for the Advancement of Science from the National Academy of Sciences.

events.title: International Prize for Biology (Japan)
events.description: Felsenstein receives the International Prize for Biology from the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

events.title: Catalog reaches 392 packages
events.description: Felsenstein's software catalog grows to list 392 phylogeny packages and 54 free web servers, the most comprehensive directory of phylogenetics software ever maintained.

events.title: PHYLIP surpasses 25,000 citations
events.description: Cumulative citations of PHYLIP across all versions exceed 25,000. Over 30,000 registered users worldwide. Still cited over 1,000 times per year.

events.title: PHYLIP version 3.696 — open source
events.description: PHYLIP adopts an open-source license for the first time, allowing redistribution alongside commercially or restrictively licensed software.

events.title: Pages migrated to GitHub
events.description: PHYLIP pages and software catalog migrated from evolution.genetics.washington.edu to phylipweb.github.io/phylip/. Felsenstein invites community help in maintaining the catalog.

events.title: PHYLIP version 3.698 released
events.description: Latest version. Consensus tree bug fix, 64-bit Windows support for Java tree-drawing front-ends.

events.title: Mendel Medal
events.description: Felsenstein receives the Mendel Medal from the U.K. Genetics Society.
